meta.notes: All content for the prototype. Onboarding shows `conditions`; the user's selection picks the scenario whose `conditions` match (Arthritis + Back pain → the combined scenario). `camera: true` scenarios get the camera set-up step and automatic step detection while cooking. A step's optional `watch` ({kind: boil | pressure | preheat, minutes}) is a camera-estimated wait shown before any timer.
meta.photoNotes: All photos are free Unsplash images (Unsplash License, no Unsplash+), checked by eye against their recipe. Each scenario's `cameraPhoto` is the one generic home stove its camera view shows for the whole session.

conditions.label: Back pain
conditions.sub: Bending to the oven, lifting pots, standing long

otherInput.voiceSample: I have arthritis in my hands and my lower back hurts when I bend down to the oven.

scenarios.label: Arthritis
scenarios.onboardingBlurb: Opening jars, gripping knives or twisting lids is painful.

persona.name: Margaret
persona.bio: Retired school teacher who loves feeding her grandkids on Sundays. Rheumatoid arthritis in both hands makes fine motor tasks hard.

constraints.title: Trouble gripping knives
constraints.detail: Chopping hard vegetables like onions and carrots causes finger pain.

constraints.title: Can't open jars or twist lids
constraints.detail: Screw tops, cans and tight lids are hard to open.

constraints.title: Morning stiffness
constraints.detail: Hands are stiffest before 10am, so she cooks later in the day.

tools.name: Rocker knife
tools.why: You rock it instead of sawing, so you need less grip strength.

tools.name: Under-cabinet jar opener
tools.why: Twists lids using your arm instead of your fingers.

tools.name: Wide-grip peeler
tools.why: A thick, soft handle spreads the pressure across your palm.

tips: Buy pre-chopped onions and frozen diced vegetables. They taste the same and save your hands.
Soak your hands in warm water for a minute before cooking to ease stiffness.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Peel and chop the carrots, onion and potatoes into bite-size pieces.
Squeeze the lemon over the chicken with the oil, thyme, salt and pepper.
Spread everything on a sheet pan and roast.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

simplified.summary: No chopping or squeezing. Everything goes on the pan straight from the bag.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line the pan with foil so cleanup is easy.
Tip the pre-cut vegetable mix and baby potatoes straight from the bag onto the pan.
Lay the chicken on top. Drizzle with oil from a squeeze bottle and sprinkle with bottled lemon juice and thyme.
Slide the pan in using both hands and roast.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve from the pan.

swaps.to: Pre-cut stir-fry or roasting veg mix

swaps.why: Easier to grip than a twist cap

prepAhead: Ask the butcher to trim the chicken
Keep a squeeze bottle of oil by the stove

steps.text: Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Melt the butter and soften the onion and garlic.
Open the cans and add the tomatoes and broth.
Simmer.
Blend until smooth, then stir in the cream and basil.

simplified.summary: Uses cartons and frozen garlic, so there are no cans or chopping. A stick blender does the blending.

steps.text: Melt the butter and add 1 cup of frozen diced onion and 1 tsp of jarred garlic, opened with your jar opener.
Pour in the carton of crushed tomatoes and the carton of broth.
Simmer with the lid off.
Blend in the pot with a stick blender, holding it with both hands.
Stir in the cream and tear in the basil with your fingers.

swaps.why: No lifting or pouring hot soup

prepAhead: Keep cartons in a low cupboard

steps.text: Combine the oats, milk, yogurt and honey in a mason jar.
Screw on the lid and shake well.
Refrigerate overnight.
Top with berries in the morning.

simplified.summary: A bowl with a snap-on lid replaces the screw-top jar.

steps.text: Add the oats, milk, yogurt and honey to a container with a snap-on lid.
Stir with a fat-handled spoon. No shaking needed.
Press the lid down with your palm and refrigerate overnight.
Add frozen berries straight from the bag in the morning.

prepAhead: Make 3 at once on a good-hands day

scenarios.label: Back Pain
scenarios.onboardingBlurb: Bending to the oven, lifting pots or standing for long is hard.

persona.name: Robert
persona.bio: Former carpenter who took over the cooking when his wife's eyesight declined. Lower back pain after 15 minutes of standing.

constraints.title: Can't stand for long
constraints.detail: Lower back aches after 15 minutes at the counter.

constraints.title: Bending to low ovens
constraints.detail: Reaching into a low oven or bottom cabinet is painful.

constraints.title: Lifting heavy pots
constraints.detail: Avoids carrying full stockpots or cast iron.

tools.name: Counter-height perching stool
tools.why: Lets you prep sitting down at counter height.

tools.name: Slow cooker
tools.why: Sits on the counter, so there's no bending to the oven.

tools.name: Countertop air fryer
tools.why: Does the oven's job at waist height.

tips: Prep sitting down and keep everything you need within arm's reach.
Fill pots where they'll cook. Use a pitcher to carry the water.

steps.text: Brown the turkey in a heavy skillet on the stove.
Chop the onion and pepper at the counter.
Lift the skillet and pour the turkey into the slow cooker.
Add everything else and cook on low.

simplified.summary: Everything goes into the slow cooker raw, and you prep sitting down. No skillet to lift.

steps.text: Sit at the counter. Put the slow cooker in front of you.
Add the raw turkey, breaking it up with a wooden spoon.
Add the frozen pepper-and-onion mix, beans, tomatoes and spices.
Stir, cover and cook on low. Go rest.
Ladle into bowls straight from the cooker.

swaps.why: No heavy pan to lift or pour

prepAhead: Keep the slow cooker on the counter, not in a low cupboard

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Mix the honey, soy and minced garlic, then brush over the salmon.
Bend down and put the tray in the oven.
Steam the green beans on the stove.

simplified.summary: The air fryer does the oven's job at waist height, and the beans cook alongside.

steps.text: Stir together the honey, soy and jarred garlic.
Brush it onto the salmon and place the salmon in the air-fryer basket with the green beans.
Air fry at 390°F (200°C).
Serve straight from the basket.

swaps.why: Fewer things to lift and wash

steps.text: Chop all the vegetables and protein.
Heat a wok over high heat.
Stir-fry in batches, tossing the wok.
Add the sauce and serve over rice.

simplified.summary: Uses an electric skillet set up at the table, so you cook sitting down and nothing needs tossing.

steps.text: Set the electric skillet on the table and heat it to 375°F.
Add the pre-cut stir-fry vegetables and pre-cubed tofu.
Stir with a long spoon while seated.
Pour in the sauce. Microwave the rice pouch.

scenarios.label: Knee Pain
scenarios.onboardingBlurb: Standing for long, squatting to low cupboards or kneeling is hard.

persona.name: Dorothy
persona.bio: Church potluck legend recovering from a knee replacement. Wants to get back to cooking her family favourites.

constraints.title: Can't stand for long
constraints.detail: Knees swell after 20 minutes on her feet.

constraints.title: Squatting to low cupboards
constraints.detail: Pots and pans are kept in the bottom drawers.

constraints.title: Fear of falling
constraints.detail: Avoids step stools and wet floors.

tools.name: Anti-fatigue mat
tools.why: Cushions your knees while you stand at the stove.

tools.name: Perching stool
tools.why: Takes weight off your knees during prep.

tools.name: Slow cooker / Instant Pot
tools.why: Hands-off cooking, so you can sit down.

tips: Move your most-used pots up to counter height.
Set timers and sit down between steps. The app will remind you.

steps.text: Get the Dutch oven from the bottom cupboard.
Brown the beef in batches, standing at the stove.
Chop the vegetables.
Simmer everything on the stove, stirring often.

simplified.summary: The Instant Pot does the work. Prep sitting down, then rest while it pressure-cooks.

steps.text: Sit at the counter. Add the beef, the pre-cut stew vegetables and the broth to the Instant Pot.
Stir in the tomato paste from a tube.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on high. Go put your feet up.
Natural release.
Ladle into bowls.

swaps.to: Instant Pot kept on the counter

prepAhead: Buy the pre-cut stew vegetable pack

steps.text: Steam the salmon over a pot of simmering water.
Cook the rice on the stove.

simplified.summary: A complete dinner made in the microwave in about 10 minutes.

steps.text: Put the salmon and the broccoli in a microwave-safe dish.
Drizzle with soy sauce and ginger paste. Cover with a vented lid.
Microwave on high.
Rest while you heat the rice pouch.
Layer the yogurt, berries and granola in a glass.
Drizzle with honey.

simplified.summary: Already simple. Just make it at the table.

steps.text: Bring a tray to the table with the yogurt, berries, granola and honey.
Layer them in a bowl while seated.

prepAhead: Wash the berries ahead and keep them in a container at eye level in the fridge

scenarios.label: Arthritis + Back pain
scenarios.onboardingBlurb: Gripping, opening jars, bending and lifting are all hard.

persona.name: Evelyn
persona.bio: Retired librarian who hosts her book club for lunch every month. Arthritis in her hands and a sore lower back mean she avoids chopping, jars and heavy pots.

constraints.title: Trouble gripping knives and lids
constraints.detail: Chopping, peeling and twisting jar lids hurt her fingers.

constraints.title: Bending to the oven
constraints.detail: Reaching into a low oven or bottom cupboard strains her lower back.

constraints.title: Lifting heavy pots
constraints.detail: Carrying a full pot of water to the sink is off-limits.

constraints.title: Standing for long
constraints.detail: Her back aches after about 15 minutes at the counter.

tools.name: Rocker knife
tools.why: You rock it instead of sawing, so you need less grip strength.

tools.name: Under-cabinet jar opener
tools.why: Twists lids using your arm instead of your fingers.

tools.name: Countertop air fryer
tools.why: Does the oven's job at waist height, so there's no bending.

tips: Buy pre-cut vegetables and cartons instead of cans and jars.
Prep sitting down with everything within arm's reach.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Open the jar of marinara and warm it in a saucepan.
Cook the pasta.
Carry the pot to the sink and drain the pasta.
Stir in the sauce and spinach, then grate parmesan on top.

simplified.summary: Everything cooks in one light pan, so there's no heavy pot to drain, no jar to open and no grating.

steps.text: Sit at the stove on your perching stool. Put a wide, light two-handled pan on the front burner.
Add the dry pasta, the carton of marinara and 2 cups of water.
Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil, then cover.
Simmer, giving it one gentle stir halfway through.
Drop in the spinach and let it wilt, then shake on the pre-grated parmesan.

swaps.from: Boil and drain a big pot

prepAhead: Keep the light pan on the stovetop so you don't bend for it

steps.text: Get the casserole dish from the bottom cupboard and preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Trim and season the chicken.
Bake the chicken over raw rice and broth.
Lift the heavy dish out of the oven and rest.

simplified.summary: The air fryer cooks the chicken at waist height and the rice comes ready-made, so there's no bending, lifting or knife work.

steps.text: Sit at the counter. Spray the boneless thighs with oil and shake on the paprika and garlic powder.
Switch on the air fryer at 380°F (195°C) to preheat.
Lay the chicken in the air-fryer basket and cook.
Microwave the rice pouch with the frozen peas in a bowl.
Let the chicken rest, then serve on the rice.

prepAhead: Ask the butcher to trim the thighs
Open rice pouches with spring-loaded scissors

steps.text: Open the can of chickpeas, then drain and rinse them.
Chop the tomatoes and cucumber at the counter.
Crumble the feta and whisk the dressing.
Toss everything together.

simplified.summary: A no-cook lunch you can make sitting at the table, with no can opener, knife or whisk.

steps.text: Bring a light bowl and the ingredients to the table on a tray.
Pour in the chickpeas from the carton.
Add the whole cherry tomatoes, sliced cucumber and crumbled feta.
Squeeze on the dressing and stir gently with a fat-handled spoon.
